title: Acute Soft Tissue Injuries and Sprains: Ottawa Rules and Referral Thresholds

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult with an acute ankle or foot soft tissue injury: Ottawa ankle and foot rules for X-ray, PRICE self-care, analgesia with paracetamol and ibuprofen, recovery time and when to seek help. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-18-tier3b-v1-live.
unverifiedSections: The Ottawa rules were read from a Scottish emergency medicine page without date or page number; the knee rule is not covered.
No national sprain guideline (NICE CKS or British National Formulary) was opened because they were not accessible; self-care and dosing are from NHS website pages.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: A sprain is a stretch or tear of a ligament; a strain involves muscle or tendon. The Ottawa rules identify which patients with malleolar or midfoot pain need X-ray. Most sprains and strains feel better after 2 weeks; severe injuries can take months. Inability to take four steps both immediately and at assessment suggests a possible fracture.

clinicalManagement.title: Apply the Ottawa rules
actions: Check exclusions, then malleolar and midfoot tenderness and four steps of weight bearing.

clinicalManagement.title: X-ray if criteria met
actions: Ankle or foot series as above.

clinicalManagement.title: Self-care for the first 2 to 3 days (PRICE)
actions: Protection, rest, ice for up to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours, compression, elevation; avoid heat, alcohol and massage in the first days.
Start gentle exercise after 2 to 3 days or sooner if improving.

clinicalManagement.title: Analgesia
actions: Start with paracetamol; ibuprofen gel, mousse or spray for swelling; oral ibuprofen if needed.

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Re-assess if not improving at 2 weeks or not significantly better at 6 to 8 weeks.
Avoid strenuous exercise such as running for up to 8 weeks.

regimens.dose: 500 to 1,000 mg per dose (1 or 2 500 mg tablets)
regimens.duration: Short course; see a doctor if pain persists
adjustments: Under 50 kg may need a lower dose.
Liver conditions can make it unsuitable; no specific hepatic adjustment is given.
Usually the preferred painkiller in pregnancy.
monitoring: Do not exceed the maximum: 8 tablets of 500 mg or 4 of 1 g in 24 hours.
contraindications: Liver conditions may make paracetamol unsuitable.
Taking too much can damage the liver.

regimens.indication: Pain and swelling from sprain or strain
regimens.dose: 200 to 400 mg per dose (200 mg: 1 or 2 tablets; 400 mg: 1 tablet)
regimens.frequency: Up to 3 times a day, at least 4 hours apart
regimens.duration: Not more than 10 days unless a doctor advises
adjustments: Maximum 6 tablets of 200 mg or 3 of 400 mg in 24 hours.
Avoid in pregnancy unless a doctor or pharmacist advises.
monitoring: See a GP if pain worsens or does not go away.
contraindications: Allergy to ibuprofen, aspirin or another NSAID; stomach ulcer or history of one; asthma; chickenpox; heart, liver or kidney conditions; blood clotting problems; previous stroke; pregnancy.
Do not combine with other NSAIDs.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Pain in the malleolar region and any of: bone tenderness along distal 6 cm of posterior edge or tip of lateral or medial malleolus, or inability to weight bear for 4 steps immediately and at assessment.
Pain in the midfoot and any of: bone tenderness at base of 5th metatarsal or navicular, or inability to weight bear for 4 steps.
Age under 18, intoxication, multiple painful injuries, pregnancy, head injury or diminished sensation from a neurological deficit.

learningObjectives: Apply exclusions then the Ottawa criteria.
Use PRICE and analgesia for the first days.
pitfalls: Using the rule in children or intoxicated patients.
